properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued September 9 at 3:21AM CDT until September 10 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM THURSDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH EARLY
THURSDAY EVENING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR SOUTHWEST
AND PORTIONS OF NORTHWEST NORTH DAKOTA...

.Warm and breezy conditions are expected over western North Dakota on
Thursday ahead of an approaching cold front. Temperatures are
forecast to climb into the upper 80s, with afternoon humidities of 12
to 20 percent. Winds on Thursday afternoon are forecast to be
westerly 15 to 25 mph with gusts to 35 mph. Due to the low humidity
and breezy conditions with abundant dry vegetation, critical fire
weather conditions are forecast to occur Thursday afternoon into
early Thursday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of northwest and southwest North Dakota.

* TIMING...From Thursday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* WINDS...West winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity from 12 and 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions are
forecast to occur. Listen for later forecast updates and a possible
upgrade of this watch to a Red Flag Warning.

strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 9 at 2:30AM CDT until September 9 at 7:30AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
FFWOAX

The National Weather Service in Omaha/Valley has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Harrison County in southwestern Iowa...
Northwestern Mills County in southwestern Iowa...
Pottawattamie County in southwestern Iowa...
Southern Shelby County in southwestern Iowa...
Southeastern Dodge County in east central Nebraska...
Douglas County in east central Nebraska...
Sarpy County in east central Nebraska...
Eastern Saunders County in east central Nebraska...
Southeastern Washington County in east central Nebraska...

* Until 730 AM CDT.

* At 230 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas. This heavy rain could
especially affect portions of north Omaha as storms train
over the area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Omaha, Council Bluffs, Bellevue, Papillion, Blair, Ralston, Wahoo,
Gretna, Bennington, Boys Town, Elkhorn, Offutt AFB, Millard, La
Vista, Carter Lake, Missouri Valley, Valley, Oakland and Avoca.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

of producing winds to around 30 knots and weak waterspouts. This
thunderstorm was located 24 nm south of Louisiana Offshore Oil Port,
or 37 nm southeast of Timbalier Island, moving west at 15 knots.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 9 at 2:08AM CDT until September 9 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Iowa...

Walnut Creek at Clive I-80/35 affecting Dallas and Polk Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Walnut Creek at Clive I-80/35, or from Little Walnut Creek
to the North Walnut Creek.

* WHEN...From early this morning to this evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Swanson Blvd is closed from Harbach Blvd
west to NW 94th St due to storm sewer backup. The intersection of
93rd St and Lincoln St is closed also due to storm sewer backup.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:58 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 8.4 feet, and rising.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
this morning to a crest of 9.8 feet this morning. It will then
fall below flood stage this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

River forecasts include observed precipitation plus forecast
precipitation over the next 24 hours.

properties.areaDesc: Kings (Brooklyn); Southwest Suffolk; Southeast Suffolk; Southern Queens; Southern Nassau
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 9 at 3:06AM EDT until September 10 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected and 4 to 7 ft surf.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...From this evening through Thursday evening.

* RIP CURRENT IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely
for all people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the
beaches should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* RIP CURRENT DETAILS...The rip current risk will be low this
morning at the ocean beaches, but increasing to moderate through
the afternoon and then high by late in the day as southerly
winds and surf increase.

* BEACH IMPACTS...Minor beach flooding is possible during the
times of high tide this evening through Thursday.
properties.instruction:
If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 9 at 1:49AM CDT until September 9 at 7:45AM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:
FFWDMX

The National Weather Service in Des Moines has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Dallas County in central Iowa...
Southern Polk County in central Iowa...
Northern Madison County in south central Iowa...
Northern Warren County in south central Iowa...
Northern Adair County in southwestern Iowa...
Northern Cass County in southwestern Iowa...
Southern Audubon County in west central Iowa...
Southern Guthrie County in west central Iowa...

* Until 745 AM CDT.

* At 149 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4.5 inches of rain
have fallen, with locally higher amounts. Additional rainfall
amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area through
sunrise. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Des Moines, West Des Moines, Ankeny, Urbandale, Johnston, Clive,
Indianola, Altoona, Waukee, Norwalk, Pleasant Hill, Grimes,
Atlantic, Adel, Guthrie Center, Windsor Heights, Carlisle,
Bondurant, Saylorville and Mitchellville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

For the latest stream observations and forecasts refer to
weather.gov/desmoines/water.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 8 at 11:31PM CDT until September 9 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 106.

* WHERE...Bosque, Fannin, Hood, Jack, Palo Pinto, Parker, Somervell,
Stephens, Young, and Lamar Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity will increase the risk
for heat-related illnesses to occur, particularly for those working
or participating in outdoor activities.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke. To
reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be
moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an emergency!
Call 911 ASAP if you or someone you know is exhibiting signs of heat
stroke.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 8 at 10:05PM CDT until September 9 at 8:20PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 26.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 PM CDT Tuesday was 26.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 18.8 feet Sunday
evening.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 26.2
feet on 03/19/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 8 at 7:33PM PDT until September 10 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures 10 to 20 degrees above
normal during the day, with overnight lows also running 10 to 20
degrees above normal.

* WHERE...Bay Area and Central Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive
to heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or
adequate hydration. Impacts possible in some health systems and
in heat-sensitive industries. Hot conditions can cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 8 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for Wednesday. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:

will produce heat index values between 108 and 111 degrees for
several hours Tuesday afternoon into Tuesday evening. A few
locations may briefly experience heat index values above 111F
degrees.

If you plan to spend time outside, drink plenty of water, wear
light weight and light colored clothing and take frequent breaks
from the heat. Young children and pets should never be left
unattended in vehicles.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 4:48PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Hydrologic Concerns:
* High water coming down Kuskokwim River, in combination with strong
south to southwesterly winds, could cause bankfull conditions or
minor flooding along the Kuskokwim and Johnson Rivers during high
tide.

Locations:
* Along Kuskokwim River, from Bethel south to Napakiak.
* Along Johnson River, from Nunapitchuk and Kasigluk south to the
Kuskokwim River.

Timing:
* Highest water levels will likely occur around high tide on Friday,
from about 11 AM through 4 PM.
* Strongest winds (south to southwesterly, gusting up to 30 to 45
mph) from about 4 PM Thursday through 4 PM Friday.

Next Steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED WATER LEVELS ALONG KUSKOKWIM AND JOHNSON RIVERS ON THURSDAY AND FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 4:41PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

For communities along Kuskokwim River (Tuntutuliak):
* High water coming down Kuskokwim River, in combination with storm
surge flowing up river, could cause bankfull conditions or minor
flooding during high tide.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide, which will
be from around 11 AM through 4 PM.

For communities along the coast (Kongiganak, Kwigillingok, Kipnuk,
Toksook Bay, Tununak):
* Strong onshore winds could bring the potential for coastal erosion
and minor coastal flooding.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide on Friday,
from about 10 AM through 2 PM. Communities further north, like
Toksook Bay and Tununak, may see higher water levels during
Thursday's high tide as well.

Next steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 8 at 2:16PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Streams draining southern slopes of the Western Brooks Range.

Incoming rainfall from a atmospheric river will bring rainfall to the
southern slopes of the western end of the Brooks Range through
Friday.  Rainfall totals may exceed two inches in some locations and
cause significant rises on small streams.

The Kobuk, Noatak, and Wulik Rivers should also see rises from this
system into the weekend, but no flooding is expected.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot late-season conditions expected with high
temperatures up to 112 to 116 in Death Valley and the Colorado
River Valley; up to 105 to 110 in the Las Vegas Valley, Moapa
Valley, and Pahrump Valley.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 8 at 11:33AM MST until September 10 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 105 to
109 expected. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...The Phoenix metropolitan area.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water, and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.
